ai.literal: With those born of noble family, except, do not exist naturally, integrity and modesty, together.
ai.translation: Integrity and a sense of shame do not naturally exist together in anyone, except in those born of noble lineage.
ai.modern: உயர்ந்த குடியில் பிறந்தவர்களிடம் அல்லாமல் மற்றவர்களிடம் நேர்மையும் நாணமும் இயற்கையாகவே ஒருசேர இருப்பதில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the defining qualities of noble birth. The poet states that uprightness (செப்பம்), which represents integrity and fairness, and modesty (நாண்), which is the healthy sense of shame that prevents one from doing wrong, naturally coexist only in those born of a noble family. In others, these two virtues do not come together as an inherent nature. The word 'செப்பம்' refers to impartiality or rectitude, while 'நாண்' refers to the shrinking back from dishonorable deeds. Together, they form the bedrock of noble character.

ai.literal: Good conduct and, truthfulness and, a sense of shame and, these, all three things, they will not fail in, noble family, those who are born.
ai.translation: Those who are born of a noble family will never fail in these three qualities: good conduct, truthfulness, and a sense of shame.
ai.modern: நற்குடியில் பிறந்தவர்கள் ஒழுக்கம், உண்மை, பழிக்கு நாணுதல் ஆகிய இந்த மூன்றிலிருந்தும் என்றும் தவற மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essential qualities of those born into a noble family. The poet lists three core virtues: right conduct, truthfulness, and a moral sense of shame that shrinks from doing wrong. Those of noble birth will never deviate or slip from these three principles, regardless of the circumstances. The word 'நாண்' here represents a deep-seated conscience rather than simple shyness, acting as a shield against dishonorable actions.

ai.literal: A smile, generosity, sweet words, and not despising others—these four, they say, are the characteristics of a truthful family.
ai.translation: A cheerful smile, generosity, pleasant speech, and freedom from contempt for others—these four are said to be the defining characteristics of a truly noble lineage.
ai.modern: மகிழ்ச்சியான முகம், கொடைத்தன்மை, இனிய சொல், பிறரை இகழாமல் இருத்தல் ஆகிய நான்கும் உண்மையான நற்குடிப் பிறந்தவர்க்குரிய இயல்புகள் என்று கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the four essential qualities that define a person of noble birth or high lineage. First is a cheerful, smiling countenance that welcomes others. Second is generosity, the willingness to give to those in need. Third is speaking kind and pleasant words. Fourth is refraining from looking down upon or despising anyone. The poet asserts that these four virtues are the defining traits of a family of genuine truthfulness and nobility.

ai.literal: Piled up ten-millions even if they obtain, those born of noble family, things that diminish character, doing, they will not.
ai.translation: Even if they were to obtain millions upon millions piled high, those born of noble lineage will never do things that diminish their character.
ai.modern: அடுக்கடுக்கான பல கோடிகளைப் பெற்றாலும், நல்ல குடியில் பிறந்தவர்கள் தம் பெருமையைக் குறைக்கும் செயல்களைச் செய்ய மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the unyielding integrity of those born into noble families. The phrase 'அடுக்கிய கோடி' refers to stacked millions, representing immense wealth. Even when tempted with or offered such vast riches, those of noble birth will never commit actions that diminish ('குன்றுவ') their high character or family honor. Their commitment to virtue and dignity is absolute and cannot be bought at any price.

ai.literal: Even when [their] capacity to give is collapsed within, [those of] ancient lineage departing from [their] noble character is not.
ai.translation: Even when their means to give have utterly diminished, those of ancient noble lineage never depart from their noble character.
ai.modern: பிறருக்குக் கொடுக்கும் கொடைத்தன்மை வறுமையினால் சுருங்கிப் போன காலத்திலும், பழமையான குடியில் பிறந்தவர்கள் தம்முடைய நற்பண்பிலிருந்து விலக மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the enduring nature of noble character in people of ancient lineage. The phrase 'valanguvathu ulveelntha' refers to a state where one's wealth and ability to practice charity have completely collapsed or shrunk. Even in such extreme adversity and poverty, those from a long line of noble ancestors ('palangudi') do not swerve ('talaippirital indru') from their innate noble qualities ('panpu'). Their nobility is defined not by their material wealth, but by their steadfast adherence to their values even when they have nothing left to give.

ai.literal: Deceit clinging to, deeds devoid of nobility they will not do, 'spotless lineage relying on we shall live' those who say.
ai.translation: Those who resolve, 'We shall live by relying on our spotless lineage,' will not perform deeds devoid of nobility, even when motivated by deceit or anger.
ai.modern: குற்றமற்ற குடிப்பிறப்பை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டு வாழ்வோம் என்று நினைப்பவர்கள், வஞ்சனையினாலோ அல்லது கோபத்தினாலோ தகுதிக்கு ஒவ்வாத செயல்களைச் செய்யமாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the self-imposed standards of those born into noble families. People who pride themselves on maintaining the spotless reputation of their lineage ('மாசற்ற குலம்') resolve to live strictly by those high standards. Consequently, even when faced with situations that provoke deceit, anger, or hostility ('சலம்'), they will never stoop to performing actions that lack dignity or nobility ('சால்பில'). Their commitment to their family's honor acts as a shield against unethical behavior.

ai.literal: The fault that appears in those born of noble family will shine out, like the spot on the moon in the sky, rising high.
ai.translation: The faults of those born in a noble family will stand out conspicuously, like the dark spot on the moon high up in the sky.
ai.modern: உயர்ந்த குடியில் பிறந்தவர்களிடம் காணப்படும் குற்றம், வானத்தில் உள்ள சந்திரனிடத்தில் இருக்கும் களங்கம் போல, எல்லோருக்கும் மிகத் தெளிவாகத் தெரியும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how even minor flaws in people of noble birth are easily noticed by the world. The author compares their faults to the dark spot on the moon. Just as the moon is high in the sky for everyone to see, noble people hold a high position in society, making their actions highly visible. Therefore, any blemish in their character stands out prominently, just like the dark spot on the bright moon.

ai.explanation: This couplet explains how essential love and affection are to a person of noble birth. The word 'நார்' literally means fiber or cord, but here it refers to the bond of affection and kindness that connects people. Even if a person possesses other good qualities, if they show a complete lack of love, people will begin to doubt the nobility of their family background. True nobility is not just about outward manners, but is fundamentally rooted in genuine love for others.

ai.literal: The sprout will reveal what lay hidden in the soil; the words from the mouth will reveal those born in a noble family.
ai.translation: Just as an emerging sprout reveals the nature of the soil in which the seed lay, the words spoken from the mouth reveal the noble lineage of those born to it.
ai.modern: நிலத்தில் புதைந்து கிடக்கும் விதையின் தன்மையை அதிலிருந்து முளைக்கும் முளை காட்டும்; அதுபோல, உயர்ந்த குலத்தில் பிறந்தவர்களின் தன்மையை அவர்கள் வாயிலிருந்து வெளிப்படும் சொல் காட்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a beautiful natural analogy to explain how a person's speech reflects their upbringing and lineage. The word 'kāl' here refers to the young sprout or shoot emerging from the earth. Just as the health and type of a sprout reveal the quality of the hidden soil in which the seed lay, the words that come out of a person's mouth instantly reveal the quality and nobility of the family they were born into. The repetition of the verb 'kāṭṭum' (will reveal) emphasizes the direct and inescapable connection between origin and expression.

ai.literal: If goodness is desired, possession of shame is required; if noble lineage is desired, let one desire humility towards everyone.
ai.translation: If one desires moral excellence, one must possess a sense of shame; if one desires to preserve a noble lineage, one must practice humility towards everyone.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் தனக்கு நன்மையை விரும்பினால் நாணத்தைக் கொண்டிருக்க வேண்டும்; தன் குலத்தின் பெருமையை விரும்பினால் எல்லாரிடமும் பணிவைக் கொண்டிருக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the essential qualities needed for personal virtue and family honor. To achieve moral goodness (நலம்), a person must have a sense of shame (நாண்) that holds them back from doing wrong. To maintain the dignity of a noble lineage (குலம்), one must cultivate humility (பணிவு) towards all people. True nobility is thus defined not by pride or birth, but by the practice of modesty and respectful humility.
